description: Name under which the product will be sold.

mandatory_item_name: Designation Class/Type or Statement of Composition
description: Class/type designation (e.g., Red Wine, Sparkling Wine, Chardonnay) or a truthful and adequate statement of composition when class is not defined in the regulations; varietal listings may serve as the class/type designation.
Area where the fruit or agricultural product used to make the wine was grown; generally mandatory when the label contains a varietal, vintage, semi-generic type, or estate-bottled claim.
Disclosure of percentage blend of American and foreign wine when the label refers to foreign wine (e.g., '50% American wine/50% French wine').
Statement of alcohol content as a percentage by volume; follow the rules for table wine and use acceptable formats/abbreviations.
Volume of wine in the container (e.g., 750 mL, 1 L); must meet approved standards of fill (see 27 CFR 4.72) and applicable exceptions.
Name and address (city and State) as listed on the permit; must follow phrases such as 'Bottled By' or 'Imported By' with no intervening text and match permit/application entries.
If total sulfur dioxide is 10 ppm or more, label must state 'Contains Sulfites' (or equivalent); 'No sulfites added' may be used only with required accompanying language.
Government health warning statement must appear exactly as prescribed, with 'GOVERNMENT WARNING' in capital letters and bold type and the prescribed wording and punctuation.
Country of origin marking required for imported wines; must comply with U.S. Customs and Border Protection requirements.
If FD&C Yellow No. 5 is used in the wine, the label must specifically disclose 'Contains FD&C Yellow No. 5'.
If cochineal extract or carmine is used, the label must specifically disclose that fact (e.g., 'Contains Carmine').
